claims.assertion: This is a safety dispute: the rider reports the driver was speeding, braking hard and overtaking on the shoulder, and the driver's own written statement contains abusive language toward the rider, calling them 'stupid' — the kind of harassment/abuse the policy removes from automated adjudication.

Because chat/statement content of this abusive and intimidation-flavoured kind is present in the case file, the correct disposition is escalation to human review with a fact summary, not an automated fare ruling.

The rider's account is that of a genuinely alarmed passenger on a completed 10.6 km trip; the rider has a clean record (661-day account, 4.6 rating, 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes in 90 days), which is consistent with a good-faith, non-repeat complaint rather than an attempt to obtain a fare refund.

The driver has a long-standing account but 455 trips in 90 days and a written statement showing hostility toward the rider; where a safety allegation is escalated, the driver's account handling (including any pattern of abuse of riders) is properly part of the same human review, so the profile facts may support an account-review request alongside escalation.

weaknesses: No independent record corroborates the complaint: the GPS facts show the trip ran 10.6 km vs 10.7 km optimal and 16.1 min vs 16 min estimated (F1, F2), i.e. no detour or overtime, and there is no traffic or speed-band data in this case to evidence hard braking, speeding or shoulder overtaking.

The complaint rests on the rider's statement alone; the driver's contrary statement 'I drove normally' (F5) and the chat messages (F3, F4) are the only other narrative, and statements lose to system records under the argument rules.

The driver's profile is strong (F7: 820-day account, 4.72 rating, 0 upheld disputes in 90 days), which the other side will use to argue the allegation is isolated and unproven, so no monetary remedy should be requested.

claims.assertion: The rider's story does not allege any threat, intimidation or abuse by the driver, so the only trigger for a safety escalation on the rider's side is absent; the sole [threat]-tagged text in the file is the driver's own written statement (F5), which is user-submitted content and is not a rider grievance.

The rider's written complaint contains no claim of a traffic accident, personal injury or dangerous-driving charge, and the file contains no accident, injury or medical record, so the SAFE-2 escalation path for collisions/injuries is not engaged by any fact in this case.
The GPS record shows the trip was driven 10.6 km against a 10.7 km optimal route, i.e. 0.1 km shorter than optimal, so there is no off-route detour and no unbilled or excess mileage on this trip.

Total trip duration was 16.1 minutes against an estimated 16 minutes, a variance of only 0.4 minutes, which is consistent with ordinary urban traffic and inconsistent with a pattern of sustained speeding and hard braking as described.
The trip was a non-metered RydeX booking charged a fixed $24.76 with no additional or unpublished items recorded, so nothing in the fare record supports a refund of any part of the fare.

The driver has 820 days on the platform, 455 trips in the last 90 days, a 4.72 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (route: 0, no-show: 0), which does not support any account-level action.
The rider has 661 days on the platform and 0 disputes filed in the last 90 days, so this is an isolated, first-time allegation with no record of prior unsafe-driving complaints against this driver.

weaknesses: The driver's own written statement calls the rider stupid and asserts 'I drove normally' (F5); the abusive wording is squarely within the harassment/abuse language of SAFE-1 and will be read against my client regardless of who filed the complaint.

F5 is a statement, not a system record: per the record-priority rule it cannot be defended against the rider's account, and the driver has produced no GPS-based evidence of his own speed profile (no speed or harsh-braking field exists in F1/F2), so he cannot positively rebut 'speeding and braking hard'.

The GPS facts F1 and F2 only show distance and total duration; they are silent on instantaneous speed and on the alleged shoulder overtaking, so the rider may argue those claims are outside the record rather than disproved by it.

The rider's contemporaneous chat messages (F3) and the driver's polite pre-pickup message (F4) show no reciprocal abuse, which will make the rider the more credible party if the tag on F5 is treated as the trigger for escalation.

My client's clean history (F7) is only a profile fact and, under the policy, profile facts may never decide the case — they can support an outcome but cannot defeat an escalation request on their own.

points.response: SAFE-1 is triggered by the presence of threats, intimidation, harassment or personal abuse anywhere in the chat record, complaint statements or driver statement — it sets no requirement that the abuse be aimed at the complaint's filing party, and the [threat]-tagged text at F5 is a personal attack on the rider ('stupid'), i.e. abuse directed at the passenger by the driver.

I do not rely on SAFE-2 and withdraw C4; my escalation request stands on SAFE-1 alone, because the rider's complaint of speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking is a dangerous-driving allegation within the safety-event scope and the file already contains abuse at F5.
Conceded as to routing: F1 shows no off-route segment and no excess mileage, so I make no RD-1/RD-2 detour claim and seek no mileage refund.

The opponent's own admission is decisive here: endorsing a 16.1-minute total (F2) says nothing about instantaneous speed or braking, since speeding and hard braking can occur within an unchanged or even slightly shorter total duration.
Agreed, and I ask for no money: there is no fare-fact record for this RydeX trip and the rider's remedy is a human safety review, not a refund, so FARE-1 is not in play.
RD-6 account-flagging is not what I seek either, so this point is moot; my escalation rests on the abuse in the record (F5) and the unresolved safety allegation, not on the driver's profile at F7.

The rider's clean profile (F6) cuts my way: a 661-day rider with 0 disputes filed and 0 upheld in 90 days is the opposite of a pattern complainant, which supports taking the first-time safety report seriously rather than dismissing it.

I concede that the rider's report of speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking is a safety allegation, and I concede that F5's abusive wording toward the rider falls within the harassment/abuse language that SAFE-1 reserves for human review; I do not contest escalation on this record.

I agree the disposition is escalation, not a fare ruling — but escalation under SAFE-1 must be a pure evidence hand-off with no monetary remedy, since SAFE-1 provides no refund, and the ride facts show the completed trip used no extra distance or time (F1: 10.6 km actual vs 10.7 km optimal; F2: 16.1 min vs 16 min), so there is nothing for FARE-1 to refund.

The rider's clean record (F6: 661 days, 4.6 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days) goes to good faith and I do not dispute it, but good faith does not supply the missing evidence: no speed, braking or lane data exists in F1 or F2, so the rider's account remains uncorroborated even at escalation, exactly as the rider's own brief admits.

The profile facts the rider cites cut against any account action: F7 shows an 820-day account, 455 trips in 90 days, a 4.72 rating and zero disputes or upheld complaints in 90 days (route: 0, no-show: 0), and RD-6 requires a case to be made out plus a prior upheld dispute before any flag_account, so no account-review request is warranted here.
